q: A scatter plot assessment is most useful for:
choices: A. Establishing a functional relationship between the IV and the DV
B. Confirming which consequence is reinforcing the problem behavior
C. Identifying temporal patterns in behavior across time blocks
D. Calculating interobserver agreement between two observers

q: A team increasingly uses a response-cost procedure because it suppresses behavior within seconds. This pattern is best explained by:
choices: A. Response substitution into another topography by the client
B. Negative reinforcement of the staff's punishing behavior
C. Ratio strain from thinning the staff's reinforcement schedule
D. Elicited aggression in the client following punishment

q: Overly narrow stimulus control is most likely to occur when:
choices: A. Reinforcement is thinned too rapidly during acquisition training
B. Training occurs with a single instructor in a single setting
C. Generalization is programmed across multiple exemplars and settings
D. The SΔ is introduced at high intensity from the first trial

q: Applying planned ignoring (withholding attention) to behavior that is actually maintained by escape from demands is likely to:
choices: A. Function as reinforcement by delivering escape from the demand
B. Convert the behavior to an automatic reinforcement function
C. Produce no change in the behavior at any point during treatment
D. Function as extinction and steadily reduce the problem behavior

q: Skinner's (1953) Science and Human Behavior is significant to the field of ABA primarily because it:
choices: A. Established the seven dimensions defining applied behavior analysis
B. Introduced errorless learning as a discrimination teaching method
C. Articulated the natural science framework within which ABA operates
D. Introduced functional analysis as an experimental assessment method

q: Pavlov's (1927) experimental work established which phenomenon as a characteristic of respondent conditioning?
choices: A. Stimulus generalization of responses to stimuli similar to the CS
B. Resistance to extinction proportional to the density of prior reinforcement
C. Response patterning determined by the schedule of reinforcement
D. Post-reinforcement pause after a fixed-ratio requirement is met

q: Written mastery criteria in a behavior program should specify:
choices: A. Only the percentage correct averaged across all trials to date
B. The minimum number of teaching trials required in each session
C. The metric, criterion value, and number of consecutive sessions
D. The therapist's qualitative judgment about the client's overall performance

q: Evidence-based practice in ABA requires integration of:
choices: A. Meta-analyses and systematic reviews of group designs only
B. Peer-reviewed publications combined with expert consensus
C. Research evidence, clinical expertise, and client preferences
D. Research evidence from peer-reviewed single-case studies alone

q: Compared with an extinction-based reductive procedure, an advantage of DRL is that:
choices: A. The behavior keeps producing reinforcement at a lower rate
B. It removes the need for ongoing response-rate data
C. It requires no rate criterion to be specified in advance
D. It eliminates the behavior more rapidly and more completely

q: A therapist says "The opposite of hot is..." and the child says "cold." The child's response is best classified as a(n):
choices: A. Tact, because 'cold' names a physical property present in the room
B. Intraverbal, because the form lacks point-to-point correspondence
C. Mand, because the child's response produces a specific reinforcer
D. Echoic, because the response follows an adult verbal stimulus

q: Informed consent in ABA practice is best characterized as:
choices: A. An ongoing process in which clients may withdraw consent at any time
B. The responsibility of the funding source rather than the treating clinician
C. Required only when a restrictive procedure is being introduced
D. A one-time signature obtained on the intake document at admission

q: In a most-to-least prompting hierarchy, training begins with:
choices: A. No prompt at all, adding prompts after three consecutive errors
B. A verbal prompt regardless of the learner’s current skill level
C. The most intrusive prompt necessary and fades toward independence
D. The least intrusive prompt, adding intrusiveness only after errors

q: The primary efficiency advantage of using a rule or instruction is that it:
choices: A. Eliminates any need for the behavior to contact natural reinforcement
B. Removes the requirement that the learner have a listener repertoire
C. Allows behavior to come under a contingency not yet directly contacted
D. Guarantees that behavior will remain sensitive to changing contingencies

q: A contingency contract is most appropriately used when the target behavior represents:
choices: A. A skill deficit for a behavior not yet in the learner's repertoire
B. A behavior that must be suppressed through response cost
C. A behavior maintained entirely by automatic reinforcement
D. A performance deficit — a behavior already in the repertoire

q: Stimulus generalization is defined as:
choices: A. The transfer of response control from a prompt to the natural SD
B. The maintenance of behavior after the intervention is fully withdrawn
C. The occurrence of a trained response to similar untrained stimuli
D. The occurrence of novel response forms to the training stimulus

q: Backward chaining is considered advantageous primarily because:
choices: A. It is the easiest chaining method to run in natural settings
B. It can be implemented without first writing a task analysis
C. The terminal reinforcer follows the last step on every trial
D. It requires fewer instructional sessions than forward chaining

q: Stokes and Baer (1977) described 'train and hope' as:
choices: A. A strategy appropriate once maintenance-phase programming begins
B. A method for recruiting natural communities of reinforcement
C. The common but inadequate default of training without programming
D. The most efficient low-effort strategy for producing generalization

q: A learner scores 95% on a receptive ID program, but the target card always sits on the left. This suggests:
choices: A. Possible restricted stimulus control by comparison position
B. An overly dense schedule of reinforcement for correct trials
C. A need to shift to delayed match-to-sample procedures
D. Mastery of the intended auditory-visual discrimination

q: Cultural humility differs from cultural competence primarily in that humility:
choices: A. Treats self-evaluation as ongoing rather than as masterable
B. Replaces the need for individualized assessment of values
C. Applies only when working with non-English-speaking families
D. Requires no examination of the analyst's own cultural values

q: Technically, an imitative response requires that the model:
choices: A. Be presented immediately after the learner’s response occurs
B. Be a vocal model rather than a motor or gestural model
C. Serve as the discriminative stimulus evoking the response
D. Be delivered only by the primary therapist in each session

q: An intervention rapidly reduces a behavior using a procedure the child's parents find demeaning and refuse to continue at home. This intervention most clearly fails on:
choices: A. The experimental control over responding
B. Interobserver agreement on the target measure
C. The social appropriateness of the procedures
D. The internal validity of the demonstrated effect

q: The motivating operation (MO) differs from the discriminative stimulus (SD) primarily in that the MO:
choices: A. Precedes the behavior while the SD follows it as a consequence
B. Is an unconditioned stimulus while the SD is always conditioned
C. Alters only negative reinforcement contingencies, not positive
D. Alters reinforcer value rather than signaling its availability
